record.title: ABLIC S-8252 Series — battery protection IC for a 2-serial-cell Li-ion / Li-polymer pack (SOT-23-6 / SNT-6A)
record.why: IDENTITY READ OFF THE VENDOR'S OWN DOCUMENT. datasheet.pdf in this folder is ABLIC's S8252_E.pdf fetched 2026-09-02 from www.ablic.com (HTTP 200, 629067 bytes, sha256 in PROVENANCE.json); its p.1 header prints verbatim '© ABLIC Inc., 2011-2019 Rev.4.0_00' and 'BATTERY PROTECTION IC FOR 2-SERIAL-CELL PACK'. Every figure in electrical.chip.json is quoted from that file with its page. WHAT THIS FOLDER IS: the REFERENCE 2S protection IC for the Microduck's NP-F550 pack (GOAL.md rung 4) — the Robot HAT is unpublished, so whether Pollen's product carries ANY protection IC, and which, is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §9). PASS here means the part is exactly identified and its sheet is on the shelf; it does not claim the part is fitted.
record.subsector_why: open vocabulary; the sheet's own words are 'BATTERY PROTECTION IC'.
record.lifecycle_why: no page fetched states a lifecycle. The datasheet is Rev.4.0_00 (2019); ABLIC's product page was not fetched.
record.origin_why: the manufacturer's own datasheet PDF was FETCHED from ablic.com and saved byte for byte as datasheet.pdf; PROVENANCE.json carries its sha256, size and URL. No standard governs a protection IC's thresholds (origin is not 'standard'); nobody has measured a physical part (not 'measured').
record.used_by_why: no ce-elec board in this design names it yet. The Robot HAT (part:microduck-robot-hat-pcb) is where a 2S protector would sit if one is fitted.
